arxiv-2012-02858.title: Strong Near-Infrared Carbon Absorption in the Transitional Type Ia SN 2015bp Journal: ApJ This paper includes data gathered with the 6.5 m Magellan Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. Facilities: Swope, Du Pont (Retrocam), NTT (EFOSC2, SOFI), NOT (ALFOSC), Gemini:Gillett (GNIRS), Gemini:So
arxiv-2012-02858.creator: S. D. Wyatt, D. J. Sand, E. Y. Hsiao, C. R. Burns, S. Valenti, K. A. Bostroem, M. Lundquist, L. Galbany, J. Lu, C. Ashall, T. R. Diamond, A. V. Filippenko, M. L. Graham, P. Hoeflich, R. P. Kirshner, K. Krisciunas, G. H. Marion, N. Morrell, S. E. Persson, M. M. Phillips, M. D. Stritzinger, N. B. Sunt
arxiv-2012-02858.description: Abstract Unburned carbon is potentially a powerful probe of Type Ia supernova (SN) explosion mechanisms. We present comprehensive optical and near-infrared (NIR) data on the “transitional” Type Ia SN 2015bp. An early NIR spectrum ( t = − t=- 9.9 days with respect to B B -band maximum) displays a striking C I λ ​ 1.

arxiv-2105-01205.title: Dirac CP phases in a 3+1 neutrino scenario with μ − τ \mu-\tau symmetry
arxiv-2105-01205.creator: Eduardo Becerra-García, Abdel Pérez-Lorenzana
arxiv-2105-01205.description: Abstract A sterile neutrino in the 3 + 1 3+1 scheme, where the sterile accounts for neutrino anomalies not explained solely by the weak active neutrinos, arises as a natural source for the breaking of the μ − τ \mu-\tau symmetry suggested by oscillation neutrino data.

arxiv-2108-03541.title: OSCAR-Net: Object-centric Scene Graph Attention for Image Attribution
arxiv-2108-03541.creator: Eric Nguyen 1, Tu Bui 2 *, Viswanathan Swaminathan 1, John Collomosse 1,2
arxiv-2108-03541.description: Abstract Images tell powerful stories but cannot always be trusted. Matching images back to trusted sources (attribution) enables users to make a more informed judgment of the images they encounter online. We propose a robust image hashing algorithm to perform such matching.

arxiv-2112-13215.title: Continual Learning for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Continuous Auditing of Financial Accounting Data
arxiv-2112-13215.creator: Hamed Hemati, Marco Schreyer, Damian Borth
arxiv-2112-13215.description: Abstract International audit standards require the direct assessment of a financial statement’s underlying accounting journal entries. Driven by advances in artificial intelligence, deep-learning inspired audit techniques emerged to examine vast quantities of journal entry data. However, in regular audits, most of the proposed methods are applied to learn from a comparably stationary journal entry population, e.g.

arxiv-2201-03891.title: A Saliency based Feature Fusion Model for EEG Emotion Estimation
arxiv-2201-03891.creator: Victor Delvigne, Antoine Facchini, Hazem Wannous, Thierry Dutoit, Laurence Ris, Jean-Philippe Vandeborre
arxiv-2201-03891.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Victor Delvigne, Antoine Facchini, Hazem Wannous, Thierry Dutoit, Laurence Ris, Jean-Philippe Vandeborre. Among the different modalities to assess emotion, electroencephalogram (EEG), representing the electrical brain activity, achieved motivating results over the last decade. Emotion estimation from EEG could help in the diagnosis or rehabilitation of certain diseases. In this paper, we propose a dual model considering two different representations of EEG feature maps: 1) a sequential based representation of EEG band power, 2) an image-based representation of the feature vectors.

arxiv-2305-08086.title: A note on an application of discrete Morse theoretic techniques on the complex of disconnected graphs
arxiv-2305-08086.creator: Anupam Mondal, Pritam Chandra Pramanik
arxiv-2305-08086.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Anupam Mondal, Pritam Chandra Pramanik. Robin Forman’s highly influential 2002 paper A User’s Guide to Discrete Morse Theory presents an overview of the subject in a very readable manner. As a proof of concept, the author determines the topology (homotopy type) of the abstract simplicial complex of disconnected graphs of order n n (which was previously done by Victor Vassiliev using classical topological methods) using discrete Morse theoretic techniques, which are purely combinatorial in nature.

arxiv-2305-09210.title: Towards Speech Dialogue Translation Mediating Speakers of Different Languages
arxiv-2305-09210.creator: Shuichiro Shimizu Chenhui Chu Sheng Li Sadao Kurohashi
arxiv-2305-09210.description: Abstract We present a new task, speech dialogue translation mediating speakers of different languages. We construct the SpeechBSD dataset for the task and conduct baseline experiments. Furthermore, we consider context to be an important aspect that needs to be addressed in this task and propose two ways of utilizing context, namely monolingual context and bilingual context.

arxiv-2311-03714.title: Loss Balancing for Fair Supervised Learning
arxiv-2311-03714.creator: Mohammad Mahdi Khalili, Xueru Zhang, Mahed Abroshan
arxiv-2311-03714.description: Abstract Supervised learning models have been used in various domains such as lending, college admission, face recognition, natural language processing, etc. However, they may inherit pre-existing biases from training data and exhibit discrimination against protected social groups. Various fairness notions have been proposed to address unfairness issues.

arxiv-2407-21129.title: Taut functors and the difference operator
arxiv-2407-21129.creator: Robert Paré
arxiv-2407-21129.description: Abstract We establish a calculus of differences for taut endofunctors of the category of sets, analogous to the classical calculus of finite differences for real valued functions. We study how the difference operator interacts with limits and colimits as categorical versions, of the usual product and sum rules.

arxiv-2501-05964.title: Recommender Systems for Social Good: The Role of Accountability and Sustainability
arxiv-2501-05964.creator: Alan Said
arxiv-2501-05964.description: Abstract This work examines the role of recommender systems in promoting sustainability, social responsibility, and accountability, with a focus on alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As recommender systems become increasingly integrated into daily interactions, they must go beyond personalization to support responsible consumption, reduce environmental impact, and foster social good.

arxiv-2505-17930.title: Self-induced transparency and optical transients in atomic vapors
arxiv-2505-17930.creator: B. S. Cartwright, S. A. Wrathmall, R. M. Potvliege
arxiv-2505-17930.description: Abstract The rapid turn-on of a strong, resonant, continuous wave laser field may trigger the formation of a transient oscillation akin to a train of damped solitons, before the vapor-field system relaxes into a stationary state. We study this transient dynamic on theoretical models of a rubidium vapor.

arxiv-2511-22717.title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining gauge theories
arxiv-2511-22717.creator: Ali Fatemiabhari, Horatiu Nastase, Carlos Nunez, and Dibakar Roychowdhury
arxiv-2511-22717.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ali Fatemiabhari, Horatiu Nastase, Carlos Nunez, and Dibakar Roychowdhury. We study holographic Krylov complexity in the Anabalón–Ross solitonic background, a top-down Type IIB solution describing a twisted-circle compactification of 𝒩 = 4 {\cal N}=4 SYM that flows to a confining, gapped three-dimensional theory. Following the proposal that the time derivative of Krylov complexity is dual to the proper radial momentum of a falling bulk particle, we analyze probe geodesics in this geometry.

britannica-1911-talisman.title: Talisman (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-talisman.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-talisman.description: Article 'Talisman' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. term synonymous with amulet (q.v.), but strictly should be applied to an inanimate object which is supposed to possess a supernatural capacity of conferring benefits or powers, an amulet being that which protects or wards off evil (see Magic).

europmc-pmc5368208.description: Background Chronic pain patients increasingly seek treatment through mindfulness meditation. Purpose This study aims to synthesize evidence on efficacy and safety of mindfulness meditation interventions for the treatment of chronic pain in adults. Method We conducted a systemati

pmc-10607090.title: Safety of Pneumatic Dilation in Older Adults with Achalasia: An International Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-10607090.creator: Nir Bar, Christopher Vélez, Trisha S Pasricha, Tamar Thurm, Dana Ben-Ami Shor, Roy Dekel, Yishai Ron, Kyle Staller, Braden Kuo, Antoni Stadnicki
pmc-10607090.description: Background: Pneumatic dilation (PD) is an effective first line treatment option for many patients with achalasia. PD use may be limited in adults with achalasia who are older than 65 because of concern for adverse events (AE), and less efficacious therapies are often utilized. We explored the periprocedural safety profile of PD in older adults.

pmc-11492666.title: Normal saline versus lactated Ringer’s solution for acute pancreatitis resuscitation, an open-label multicenter randomized controlled trial: the WATERLAND trial study protocol
pmc-11492666.creator: Lucía Guilabert, Karina Cárdenas-Jaén, Alicia Vaillo-Rocamora, Ana García García de Paredes, Ankit Chhoda, Sunil G Sheth, Carlos López-Valero, Pedro Zapater, Eva M Navarrete-Muñoz, Patrick Maisonneuve, Yasmin G Hernández-Barco, Gabriele Capurso, James L Buxbaum, Enrique de-Madaria, for the ERICA con
pmc-11492666.description: BackgroundSome evidence suggests that fluid resuscitation with lactated Ringer’s solution (LR) may have an anti-inflammatory effect on acute pancreatitis (AP) when compared to normal saline (NS) and may be associated with a decrease in severity, but existing single-center randomized controlled trials showed conflicting results.

pmc-11587674.title: Influenza vaccination in patients with acute heart failure (PANDA II): study protocol for a hospital-based, parallel-group, cluster randomized controlled trial in China
pmc-11587674.creator: Yiqun Zhang, Rong Liu, Yangyang Zhao, Zhiyan Wang, Chi Wang, Qiang Li, Dorothy Han, Craig S. Anderson, Xin Du, Jianzeng Dong
pmc-11587674.description: BackgroundInfluenza vaccination confers broad benefits in the elderly and certain high-risk populations, but its effectiveness in patients with acute heart failure (HF) is uncertain. Rates of influenza vaccination are low in China due to poor awareness, cultural misunderstandings, and cost.AimsTo determine the effectiveness of influenza vaccination in patients with acute HF admitted to hospitals in China.

pmc-12624125.title: Green synthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles and calcined biowaste for sustainable electrodes in asymmetric supercapacitors
pmc-12624125.creator: Serra Ersoy, Mohamad Hasan Aleinawi, Emre Erdem, Figen Kaya, Cengiz Kaya, Bahattin Koc
pmc-12624125.description: Green synthesis is increasingly popular due to the focus on sustainability and biowaste recycling. This study explores zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) synthesized using broccoli extract, with carbon powder derived from calcined broccoli pulp as an alternative to commercial carbon in electrochemical slurries.

pmc-12631798.title: Edge and defect effects on charge distribution in collapsed MoS2 nanotubes
pmc-12631798.creator: Matjaž Malok, Janez Jelenc, Anja Pogačnik Krajnc, Maja Remškar
pmc-12631798.description: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) has emerged as a promising material for next-generation electronics and optoelectronic devices. MoS2 nanotubes (NTs) and their collapsed ribbon-like shapes (collapsed NTs) synthesized via chemical vapour transport (CVT) under chemical equilibrium typically exhibit low structural defect densities.

pmc-13133356.title: Non-linear and switchable light preferences of nocturnal loach (Misgurnus anguillicaudatus)
pmc-13133356.creator: Yuki Yoshikawa, Keiko Okano, Toshiyuki Okano
pmc-13133356.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Light conditions have substantial effects on living organisms through a variety of aspects of individual life, such as survival, feeding, reproduction, stress responses, and behavioral rhythms. In this study, to evaluate the importance of light conditions for nocturnal fish, the spontaneous spatial preferences and swimming activity of the loach (Misgurnus anguillicaudatus), a nocturnal freshwater fish, was investigated using controlled light intensity gradients.

pmc-13429918.title: Potential of biosynthesized nanoparticles as disinfectants against microbial contamination of chicken eggshells
pmc-13429918.creator: Mária Vargová, Ľudmila Balážová, Ľudmila Tkáčiková, Peter Váczi, František Zigo, Yaroslav Shpotyuk, Kamil Szmuc, Grzegorz Gruze, Ladislav Takáč, Zdenka Bedlovičová
pmc-13429918.description: Biosynthesized silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) exhibit antibacterial activity and can be applied by spraying for the disinfection of the external eggshell surface. This study evaluated the effects spraying of Ag NPs synthesized using Stachys recta L. extract on eggs from Plymouth Rock chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus).

uslaw-usc-t39-s1004.title: 39 U.S.C. § 1004 — Supervisory and other managerial organizations
uslaw-usc-t39-s1004.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t39-s1004.description: United States Code, Title 39 (Postal Service); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 10 (Employment Within The Postal Service). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) It shall be the policy of the Postal Service to provide compensation, working conditions, and career opportunities that will assure the attraction and retention of qualified and capable supervisory and other managerial personnel; to provide adequate and reasonable differentials.
